summary: fetch_with_retry's per-attempt timeout drops from 30s to 5s while its attempt count rises from 1 to 4, changing both individual request timing and the overall retry behavior.

items.title: Per-attempt timeout drops from 30s to 5s
items.statement: The per-attempt timeout passed to session.get drops from 30 seconds to 5 seconds.

items.title: The loop now retries instead of trying once
items.before: max_attempts was 1, so the for loop ran the request exactly once with no retry.
items.after: max_attempts is 4, so the loop retries the request up to three more times after a TimeoutError before giving up.
items.statement: max_attempts changes from 1 to 4, so a request that times out is now retried instead of immediately raising.

items.title: Worst-case time before giving up changes
items.before: With one 30s attempt and no retries, the worst case before raising TimeoutError was about 30 seconds.
items.after: With four 5s attempts and a 1s sleep between each, the worst case before raising TimeoutError is about 5*4 + 1*3 = 23 seconds.
items.statement: Combining the shorter timeout with more attempts changes the worst-case time before fetch_with_retry gives up from about 30 seconds to about 23 seconds, since the loop and sleep structure are otherwise unchanged.
